commits.message:
fix(table): draw the header row with the head characters (rich-table-6uy.2)

A heavy-framed table drew its header cells with the body verticals —
`│ A │ B │` where Rich renders `┃ A ┃ B ┃` — because _renderRow emitted
box.left/vertical/right unconditionally and headLeft/headVertical/headRight
had no reader anywhere in src/.

The header row and every body row come out of that one code path, so the
head glyphs have to be selected per row or the body goes heavy too. The
level crosses as a value: _renderRow takes a RowLevel and Box answers with
the glyphs, mirroring the getRow(widths, level) call beside it. Box keeps
both halves of the level -> glyph mapping, so rich-table-6uy.3 edits one
switch rather than hunting a second copy in Table.

HEAVY_HEAD is the only prebuilt box whose head verticals differ from its
body's, so it is the only frame that changes; verified by walking every
exported Box. docs/tables.md's flagship example already showed this output
and was a lie about the library until now.

Tests pin the default frame end to end and the footer row's verticals; the
footer test asserts content rows only, since the separators around it are
the Box's one separator set that .3 replaces. All five went red on revert.

chore(lit): refresh the embedded lit integration block and /next skill

`lit init` rewrites the block it owns in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md — the
marker rename (LINKS -> LIT) and the reworded quickstart pointer — and
writes the /next skill it now ships into .claude/skills/. Tool output,
committed as its own change so it does not ride along in a fix.

fix(box): join the header to the body with the separator glyphs (rich-table-6uy.1) (#91)

* fix(box): join the header to the body with the separator glyphs (rich-table-6uy.1)

A `Box` names its header CONTENT row verticals `head*` and its head-to-body
SEPARATOR glyphs `mid*`. `getRowChars` read "head" as "the head separator" and
reached for the verticals, so every table drew `┃━━━┃━━━┃` where the frame
wanted `┡━━━╇━━━┩` — wrong, but symmetric enough to read as plausible box art.

The glyph data was already right; only the field selection was wrong.

All four `RowLevel` arms now return the same tuple, because a `Box` carries one
separator set where Rich carries three (head_row, row, foot_row). That gap is
real and visible with `showLines`, where row separators draw the head-to-body
glyphs instead of `├───┼───┤`; it belongs to rich-table-6uy.3, which adds the
data. The arms are kept apart for it to fill.

The old tests pinned the defect and named the fields they expected, so they
could only ever pass by preserving it. Replaced with assertions on the rendered
separator. Reverting the fix turns all five red — checked, not assumed.

docs/tables.md's width ladder showed the old separator row; regenerated from
the renderer rather than redrawn by hand.

* docs(box): stop the getRowChars comment describing a reader that does not exist

The comment said `head*` holds the header content row's verticals "drawn by
the row renderer." No such wiring exists: _renderRow emits box.left and
box.vertical unconditionally, and after the separator fix nothing in src/
reads headLeft, headVertical, or headRight at all.

A caption naming a mechanism the code does not have is worse than no caption,
so the false clause is dropped rather than expanded. Wiring headVertical into
the header content row is rich-table-6uy.2, not this change.
